question: Toxoplasma gondii is the most common identifiable cause of posterior uveitis (chorioretinitis) worldwide, typically presenting as a focal area of active white retinitis adjacent to an old pigmented chorioretinal scar.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Toxoplasma gondii causes the majority of posterior uveitis cases worldwide. The classic fundus sign is a fresh white satellite lesion of active chorioretinitis adjacent to an old pigmented scar — distinguishing it from other causes. Treatment involves pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + folinic acid ('classic triple therapy') or clindamycin-based regimens.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Toxoplasmic chorioretinitis is the leading cause of posterior uveitis globally. The pathognomonic appearance is a satellite lesion — an active, fluffy white area of retinitis ('headlight in the fog' on funduscopy) adjacent to an old, pigmented, well-defined chorioretinal scar from a prior episode. Most cases represent reactivation of congenitally acquired infection.
